grade.first_issue: The first decisive defect is the claim that cases with a_{n+1}=m(H)>m^* can occur only finitely often because \mathcal M_n is finite. This is false: for a_1=2 the sequence is a_n=2n, and whenever n+1=p is prime, H={2,p} achieves a_{n+1}=m(H)=2p>m^*=2. Thus the asserted eventual reduction to a fixed finite family of hitting sets is unsupported, invoking Rule E.
grade.summary: The hitting-set reformulation and the conditional finite-state periodicity argument are meaningful progress. However, the proof never establishes its essential fixed finite family of moduli; doing so is the main structural difficulty of the problem. Moreover, even its conditional argument yields the translation law only eventually. The final statement that T and L can be enlarged to absorb an arbitrary initial transient is invalid and leaves the required conclusion for every positive n unproved, so Rule D also caps the score at 3.
strengths: Correctly translates the gcd conditions into hitting-set language and observes that the hitting-set families are nested.
The minimum products m_n are nondecreasing and can be bounded using P_1 as a hitting set, so their eventual stabilization is essentially valid.
Assuming a fixed finite family of relevant moduli, the lcm-equivariance of f and the resulting eventual periodicity of the increments are correctly described.

errors.description: The assertion that equality cases a_{n+1}=m(H)>m^* occur only finitely often does not follow from finiteness of \mathcal M_n and is demonstrably false. Consequently, no proof is given that all future transitions are controlled by a fixed finite collection \mathcal S_N. This is an unsupported central structural claim under Rule E.

The argument establishes at most an eventual relation a_{n+T}=a_n+L. Merely choosing larger T and L cannot in general make such a relation hold throughout a finite initial transient. The required all-n quantifier is therefore unhandled, invoking Rule D.
